Persons living in designated residential (CDBG) project areas; and displaced as the result of inspection and declaration of said dwelling as being insufficient in size to accommodate present occupants in accordance with existing health and safety standards, in addition to declaration of said dwelling as one requiring demolition.
Items a, b, and c above shall apply to both an owner-occupant and a tenant-occupant without regard to income.
Assistance for temporarily Displaced Owner-Occupants and Tenant-Occupants

The Housing Division shall determine that temporary housing is needed when the rehabilitation work to be done is so extensive that it cannot be reasonably undertaken without vacation of the property or when the uses of any or all of the cooking, bathroom, or sleeping facilities are prohibited.
Assistance may include:
a. Temporary placement into a hotel, motel, or apartment for a predetermined period of time.
b. Temporary food allowance of up to $12.00 per day per person for a predetermined period of time.
c. Moving costs and/or temporary storage of furniture.
d. Preparation of a rent stabilization agreement for absentee owners to limit the amount of rent increase for the tenants to not more than the monthly payments required under the terms of the rehabilitation loan.
The owner-occupant and/or tenant-occupant may or may not accept City assistance.
